findings.reason: Untrusted source: a MAC802154_HWSIM_CMD_SET_EDGE generic-netlink doit (registered with .flags = GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM, line 621, reachable from unprivileged user namespaces) whose attribute set is fully attacker-chosen. Violated invariant: the presence guard in hwsim_set_edge_lqi (lines 531-533) joins two negated presence tests with && instead of ||, so it returns -EINVAL only when BOTH required attributes are absent; a message that includes MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_ID but omits MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_EDGE passes validation while info->attrs[MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_EDGE] stays NULL (hwsim_genl_policy line 581 declares it as plain { .type = NLA_NESTED }, not NLA_POLICY_REQUIRED/NLA_NESTED with validation_data, so genl core does not reject its absence). Unsafe use: the NULL slot is passed as the nesting attribute to nla_parse_nested_deprecated at line 535, which calls nla_len()/nla_data() on it -> NULL-pointer dereference oops; additionally the inner slots edge_attrs[MAC802154_HWSIM_EDGE_ATTR_ENDPOINT_ID] and [.._LQI] are dereferenced at lines 543-544 (nla_get_u32/nla_get_u8) under a second inverted && guard at 538-540, so omitting exactly one inner attribute gives a second NULL deref even when the outer attribute is present. This is the seed mechanism (commit 0303b30375df fixed only the hwsim_del_edge_nl sibling at lines 483-487, which this snapshot already contains with ||) surviving in the adjacent SET_EDGE handler. Counterevidence checked: genl core enforces only policy type/len for present attributes, not presence, absent .required; no other guard between 531 and 535; local DoS impact (kernel oops), not a proven privilege escalation.

Same mechanism in the sibling handler hwsim_new_edge_nl (MAC802154_HWSIM_CMD_NEW_EDGE, .flags = GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM at line 609): the guard at lines 421-423 uses && over negated presence tests (logical inversion), the policy does not mark RADIO_EDGE required, so a message with RADIO_ID present and RADIO_EDGE absent reaches line 425 where the NULL info->attrs[MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_EDGE] is passed as the nesting attribute to nla_parse_nested_deprecated (NULL deref inside nla_len/nla_data of __nla_validate_parse). Even with RADIO_EDGE present, line 431 nla_get_u32(info->attrs[MAC802154_HWSIM_ATTR_RADIO_ID]) is unguarded, so omitting RADIO_ID while supplying RADIO_EDGE also crashes. Neither this handler nor hwsim_set_edge_lqi received the fix that hwsim_del_edge_nl got in the seed commit. Counterevidence checked: no required flag in hwsim_genl_policy (lines 579-582); no intervening check between guard and use.

limitations: Coverage is bounded to nested-parse/validate/for_each call sites whose nesting attribute is directly indexed from info->attrs[N]/tb[N]/attrs[N] (grep over all 145 files that use these helpers; every such parse/validate site and the for_each sites with adjacent nested parses were read).

Call sites where the nesting attribute reaches the helper through an intermediate local variable rather than direct attrs[]/tb[] indexing were not exhaustively traced (only the highest-signal subsystems were spot-checked); remaining unchecked sites are mostly dump/notify builders that construct attributes kernel-side.

No compilation or reproducer was run: the snapshot tree has no top-level Makefile/Kconfig and the assigned tree is read-only; the NULL-deref conclusion rests on reading nla_parse_nested_deprecated's use of nla_len/nla_data on the passed attribute and on genl core not enforcing presence for non-required policy entries.

Privilege reachability is asserted from .flags = GENL_UNS_ADMIN_PERM (unprivileged user-namespace admin can satisfy CAP_NET_ADMIN in userns); whether the mac802154_hwsim module is loaded in a target configuration is deployment-dependent.
Impact is characterized as local DoS (kernel NULL-pointer oops); no privilege-escalation path was demonstrated.
